dossier.public_summary: The 14-day dip is much deeper in two sectors (around 1500 ppm) and almost absent in the others (as low as -200 ppm), and the depth of individual transits varies by an order of magnitude, with the signal driven by just three deep events. A second dip of similar depth midway in the orbit is also present. Together this points to an eclipsing binary or blended false positive rather than a stable, 1.4-Earth-radius planet on the target.

reasons.why: Depth changes by a factor of several across and within sectors, expected depth 353.5 ppm; sector depths range from -204 ppm to 1534 ppm with chi2 274.8 on 7 dof. Not an aperture/calibration offset.
Depth change persists within SPOC 2-min (p_constant 1.8487656560516617e-29, sectors 6) and TESS-SPOC (p_constant 6.450383518888426e-21), ruling out pipeline offsets as cause.

Individual transits inconsistent (chi2 426.018 on 14 dof); mean 337 ppm vs sector means 146 ppm and 691 ppm. Top 3 transits carry share_of_top_3 0.878 and are ~5x deeper (~1851 ppm at epoch -64, 1628 ppm at epoch 51). Single outlier at btjd 2761.76 is -301 ppm, indicating some sectors show no dip.

Second dip detected at phase 0.5493 with depth_ppm 150.5 and depth_over_dip 0.4423, snr_at_half 0.258 and best_brightening_snr 5.2 (secondary_over_bump 1.03). Depth ratio 0.4423 is far above a planetary occultation and indicates stellar eclipse, consistent with EB at same period despite odd_even.diff_sigma 0.9817 showing no odd/even difference.

Difference imaging gives no sector with a clear difference image, cannot rule out neighbour; neighbours.plausible_within_1px 0 shows no close pixel-scale blend but centroid_all not_run leaves location untested. Planet rank 0.21 and duration_ratio 0.8774 are planet-like metrics but are outweighed by depth instability and the equal-depth secondary.
